brief: An aluminium stepped shaft on one axis: a section 20 mm in diameter and 30 mm long, followed by a section 12 mm in diameter and 40 mm long. It carries no load, so there is no load case.

intent.summary: A two-diameter stepped cylindrical shaft on a single axis, apparently intended as a non-load-bearing spacer, locator, or placeholder component rather than a power/load-transmitting shaft.
stated: First section: 20 mm diameter, 30 mm long
Second section: 12 mm diameter, 40 mm long
No load case to be considered
implied: Two sections are coaxial and joined end-to-end given it's described as a single stepped shaft
The step between 20 mm and 12 mm sections implies a shoulder/fillet transition exists, since no transition geometry was specified
Being called a 'shaft' implies it is meant to rotate or be supported in bearings/bores at some point, even though the brief says it carries no load
unstated: Which aluminium alloy/temper (affects stiffness, fatigue, corrosion resistance) is not specified
Surface finish requirements on the diameters (e.g. for bearing fit or sliding contact) not given
Tolerances on the two diameters and lengths not given
Shoulder/fillet radius or chamfer at the step transition not specified
End conditions (e.g. threaded ends, keyways, retaining ring grooves, center-drilled holes) not specified
How the shaft is supported or mounted (bearings, bushings, clamped) not specified, despite 'no load' claim
Concentricity/runout requirements between the two sections not specified
Whether the shaft rotates, is static, or is purely a dimensional placeholder not specified
Operating environment (temperature, humidity, exposure to fluids) not specified
Any coating or anodizing requirement not specified
risk_signals: None stated in the brief itself (no mention of carrying a person, lifting, pressure, stored energy, or vehicle/regulated use)

The claim 'carries no load' is asserted without context -- if this shaft is later installed in an assembly where it does bear load (e.g. support, impact, or vibration), the stated absence of a load case could mask a real hazard; this should be flagged if the end-use context changes

requirements.statement: The finished shaft's overall width (X) shall equal the largest section diameter, 20 mm.
requirements.rationale: A round part's bounding box in X equals its largest outer diameter.

requirements.statement: The finished shaft's overall depth (Y) shall equal the largest section diameter, 20 mm.
requirements.rationale: A round part's bounding box in Y equals its largest outer diameter, the same number as X.

requirements.statement: The finished shaft's overall length (Z) shall equal the sum of both section lengths, 70 mm.
requirements.rationale: The shaft's total length along its axis is the sum of the 30 mm and 40 mm sections (Z is up/along the shaft axis).

requirements.statement: The first (larger) section of the shaft shall be 20 mm in diameter.
requirements.rationale: Brief states the first section is 20 mm in diameter.

requirements.statement: The first section of the shaft shall be 30 mm long.
requirements.rationale: Brief states the first section is 30 mm long.

requirements.statement: The second (stepped-down) section of the shaft shall be 12 mm in diameter.
requirements.rationale: Brief states the second section is 12 mm in diameter.

requirements.statement: The second section of the shaft shall be 40 mm long.
requirements.rationale: Brief states the second section is 40 mm long.

requirements.statement: The part shall be round about its axis.
requirements.rationale: The brief gives this part's size as a diameter, or calls it round.

assumptions.statement: The shaft shall be made from a general-purpose aluminium alloy, e.g. 6061-T6, since the brief does not specify an alloy or temper.
assumptions.rationale: 6061-T6 is the conventional default for a non-critical aluminium machine component with no stated load case.
assumptions.consequence_if_wrong: A different alloy would change stiffness, fatigue life and corrosion resistance, but since the part carries no load this has negligible functional impact.

assumptions.statement: The step between the 20 mm and 12 mm sections will include a small transition fillet or chamfer sized to standard shaft-turning practice, since no transition geometry is specified.
assumptions.rationale: A sharp internal corner at a diameter step is not standard turning practice; a small fillet is the conventional default.
assumptions.consequence_if_wrong: If a specific fillet/chamfer size or a sharp square shoulder was actually required, the step geometry would need to be revised, but this has no functional consequence for an unloaded part.

assumptions.statement: Standard general machining tolerances apply to the stated diameters and lengths, as none are specified.
assumptions.rationale: No fits, bearings or mating parts are described, so there is no basis for tighter tolerances.
assumptions.consequence_if_wrong: If the shaft must later fit a bearing or bore, tolerances would need to be tightened, but this does not affect the current design intent.

assumptions.statement: A standard as-turned surface finish is assumed on both diameters, since no finish or sliding/bearing-fit requirement is stated.
assumptions.rationale: No rotating or sliding contact is described in the brief; a standard finish is the conventional default.
assumptions.consequence_if_wrong: If the shaft is later used in a bearing or sliding fit, a finer finish would be required, but this does not affect the stated geometry.

assumptions.statement: The two sections are coaxial on a single shared axis, as described by the brief's single-axis stepped shaft language.
assumptions.rationale: The brief explicitly describes a single-axis stepped shaft with two sections in series.
assumptions.consequence_if_wrong: An offset axis would be a fundamentally different part, but the brief gives no indication of this.

document.name: Stepped shaft 20/12
document.description: A single-axis stepped cylindrical shaft: a 20 mm diameter by 30 mm long section joined to a 12 mm diameter by 40 mm long section, with a small transition fillet at the step. Non-load-bearing per brief.

parameters.description: Small fillet at the diameter step, per standard turning practice (ASM_FILLET); not stated in the brief, chosen conservatively small relative to the 12 mm section

features.description: First (larger) section, 20 mm diameter by 30 mm long, from z=0
Second (stepped-down) section, 12 mm diameter by 40 mm long, stacked on top of section1
Join the two coaxial sections with a small transition fillet at the step

answer.rationale: The shaft is two coaxial cylinders (section1, larger, from z=0; section2, smaller, stacked on top at z=section1_length) joined by a single union whose blend_radius parametrically drives the step's transition fillet (ASM_FILLET). All four required parameters (section1/2 diameter/length) directly size the cylinders, so bounding_box_x/y equal section1_diameter and bounding_box_z equals section1_length+section2_length automatically, and the terminal union is the single round solid the roundness check expects.
